thesis: August 3 was a broad net-loss session: 14 closed positions produced INR -809.79 gross, INR 815.81 in charges, and INR -1,625.60 net. Fresh Breakout caused INR -1,424.58 of the loss with four losing trades, while Momentum Runner added INR -125.11. Across the seven available transaction dates ending August 3, Momentum Runner is the clearest recurring setup-level problem; Fresh Breakout also loses money in aggregate but has material profitable counterexamples, so its entry-floor change remains lower confidence. Until entry quality improves, a simulation-only 0.5 position-multiplier ceiling is a defensible drawdown-control change, not a profitability fix.

selectedDay.exitSummary: Targets were effective (4 exits, INR 1,038.47 net), but Time / No progress exits lost INR 1,424.58 and carried INR 2,381.04 of day-close opportunity loss. Stops lost INR 1,240.34. The stored exit benchmark has 100% coverage, but it is an end-of-day comparison rather than an executable counterfactual.

limitations: This is an analytics-only review. No Replay, backtest, sweep, or targeted settings trial was run.

August 3 contains 187 snapshots, of which 182 are usable, under one settings fingerprint. July 30 and July 31 have materially lower usable coverage and multiple settings fingerprints, which weakens direct comparability.
Repeated snapshot appearances were not counted as independent observations; confidence uses reconciled positions and exit legs.

Transaction rows do not identify which Fresh Breakout eligibility path admitted each trade, so a score-floor recommendation may not affect strong-breakout or relaxed-path entries below the normal floor.
Exit opportunity figures compare the recorded exit with the stored day-close price; they do not prove that a later executable exit would have achieved that price.

recommendations.description: Allows Momentum Runner candidates to open new simulation trades.
recommendations.rationale: Pause new Momentum Runner entries because the setup has persistently negative net expectancy and loss concentration across the full seven-session window.
evidence: Affected group: all 33 Momentum Runner positions across 7 dates; 9 wins, INR -2,795.66 gross, INR 1,758.51 charges, INR -4,554.17 net, INR -138.01 expectancy, profit factor 0.25.
Unaffected group: the other 58 setup positions; 18 wins, INR 1,956.76 gross, INR 4,179.32 charges, INR -2,222.56 net, INR -38.32 expectancy, profit factor 0.80.
Five of seven dates support the pause: July 27, July 28, July 29, July 31, and August 3 were negative. July 24 and July 30 contradict it, but only by INR 117.66 and INR 138.20 respectively.

Losses are not isolated to late entries: 20 non-late positions lost INR 3,281.10 and 13 late positions lost INR 1,273.07. VWAP exits alone lost INR 2,898.20 across 11 exits; Stop and No progress exits lost another INR 2,651.90.
recommendations.risk: Disabling the setup would also remove its profitable July 24 and July 30 trades and any future recovery. This is a temporary capital-allocation response to poor observed expectancy, not proof that the rules can never work.

validation.reason: High confidence under the seven-session rubric: 33 affected transactions across 7 dates, aggregate evidence is strongly favorable to pausing, and 5 of 7 dates (71.4%) support it. The two contradictory dates are small relative to the aggregate INR 4,554.17 loss. No replay validation was performed.

recommendations.description: Hard ceiling for the portfolio-level simulation position multiplier; 1 prevents sizing above the normal risk budget.
recommendations.rationale: Temporarily cap simulation sizing at half of the normal risk budget while setup expectancy is negative. This aims to reduce absolute loss and drawdown, not to make losing entries profitable.
evidence: Observable affected proxy: 47 positions above INR 50,000 exposure across all 7 dates; 14 wins, INR -4,985.66 net, and INR 3,992.58 in charges.
The 44 positions at or below INR 50,000 also lost money, but less in absolute terms: INR -1,791.07 net with INR 1,945.25 charges.
The above-INR-50,000 group was negative on 5 of 7 dates: July 24, July 27, July 28, July 29, and August 3. It was positive on July 30 and July 31.
On August 3, all four positions above INR 50,000 were Fresh Breakout losses totaling INR -1,424.58.
recommendations.risk: The transaction record does not store each trade's uncapped planned multiplier, so exposure above INR 50,000 is only a proxy for the exact affected population. The cap would also reduce profitable full-size trades, including the strong July 30 session, and would not improve percentage expectancy.

validation.reason: Medium confidence: 47 observable high-exposure positions across 7 dates and 5 of 7 dates support lower risk, but two profitable dates and incomplete planned-sizing fields prevent high confidence. No replay validation was performed.

recommendations.description: Independent minimum score for normal fresh-breakout entries; momentum runners use their own score thresholds.
recommendations.rationale: Research a stricter normal Fresh Breakout score floor because the observed 60-to-71 score band has negative expectancy, but preserve the current setting until the stored data identifies the exact eligibility path for each entry.
evidence: Exact score-band review: 13 Fresh Breakout positions with recorded scores from 60 through 71 across 3 dates; 3 wins and INR -1,351.10 net. All three dates containing this band were net negative for it.
The comparison group at score 72 or higher had 8 positions across 3 dates, 2 wins, and INR 481.93 net.
August 3 contributed three score-60-to-71 Fresh Breakout losses totaling INR -868.27; the score-72 WONDERLA trade also lost INR 556.31, showing that 72 is not a sufficient quality guarantee.
Material contradictory symbols exist inside the affected band, especially LUPIN at score 66 (INR 1,040.87 net) and INFY at score 68 (INR 478.64 net).
recommendations.risk: The normal minimum-score key may not govern strong-breakout or relaxed-path entries, and the affected band contains two large winners. Raising the floor could remove upside without blocking every low-score entry. Keep the current value at 60 unless future evidence records the admission path and confirms the mechanism.

validation.reason: Low confidence despite 13 affected transactions across 3 dates: the affected group is net negative and every represented date supports tightening, but material profitable counterexamples and missing eligibility-path fields make the exact key/value mechanism uncertain. No replay validation was performed.
